page: Microsoft Azure E64-32ds_v5 is an EDSv5-family virtual machine powered by an Intel Xeon 8370C processor running at 2.8 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. This server features 32 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 16 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. It is equipped with 512 GB of RAM, providing a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 16 GB per vCPU. Storage is bundled with 2458 GB of local SSD, and the instance runs on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor.

Benchmark evaluations place this server in the average tier for most compute and memory tasks, with a Geekbench single-core score of 1697.0 and a multi-core score of 14288.0. It demonstrates strong performance in image processing and memory operations, as evidenced by a Passmark memory score of 2902.8. Large block memory bandwidth reaches 149.6 GB/sec for read-only operations and 66.85 GB/sec for writes. However, CPU-bound large language model inference is a notable bottleneck, with the 70B model prompt processing speed registering at a weak 6.43 tokens/sec.

The E64-32ds_v5 offers high resource density, combining massive memory capacity with substantial local SSD storage. This profile is qualitatively cost-efficient for memory-intensive workloads that do not require high-end GPU acceleration. The server is well-suited for large-scale database operations, in-memory caching systems like Redis, data warehousing, and memory-bound enterprise applications.

It features 2458 GB of local SSD storage and operates under the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. Benchmarks indicate average overall compute performance, with a Geekbench multi-core score of 14288.0, but strong results in image processing and memory-specific tests. The high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 16 GB per vCPU and large local storage make this instance highly suitable for memory-intensive workloads, such as database hosting, caching, and data analytics, though it exhibits weak performance in large-scale LLM inference tasks.
